Why Dreams?","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":281,"printedEnd":290,"pdfStart":299,"pdfEnd":308,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep serves more than one proposed function, including energy conservation and contributions to memory. Different species show different patterns, providing clues about the constraints shaping sleep."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module compares proposals about the functions of REM sleep and the origins of dreams, including activation-synthesis and neurocognitive views. Notice what each theory explains and what questions remain."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-3-study-1","text":"Why organisms sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep is widespread across species, but its duration, posture, and organization differ considerably. Proposed functions include conserving energy, supporting restoration and regulation, and contributing to learning and memory. Evidence does not require sleep to have exactly one benefit for every species. Evolution may have added several functions to an older biological pattern. The important task is to compare predictions of different explanations rather than treating one appealing story as final."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-3-study-2","text":"Sleep and memory"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some kinds of learning benefit from periods of sleep after practice. Sleep may influence stabilization, reorganization, or selective retention of information. These findings do not mean every memory is stored only during sleep or that extra sleep guarantees perfect learning. Study the difference between observing that sleep improves performance and establishing which sleeping brain events produce the benefit."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-3-study-3","text":"REM sleep and dreams"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"REM sleep has distinctive patterns of activity and muscle inhibition. The function of REM remains debated, and findings from deprivation and cross-species comparisons need cautious interpretation. The activation-synthesis hypothesis emphasizes how the brain interprets internally generated activity; neurocognitive approaches consider ongoing cognitive networks and the organization of dream experience. Both attempt to explain dreams through brain processes but differ in emphasis."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-3-study-4","text":"An evidence-based conclusion"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep, REM, and dreaming are related phenomena but should not be collapsed into a single question. A useful revision answer separates the function of sleep overall, the specific role of REM physiology, and the origin or meaning of dream experiences. The textbook emphasizes the limits of current understanding, so a strong answer presents hypotheses as hypotheses rather than universal facts."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h01","text":"Functions of Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, we rest our muscles and decrease metabolism.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Fluid drains from the brain and spinal cord into the subarachnoid space, removing potentially harmful proteins and waste products .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People who don’t get enough sleep react more severely than average to stressful events .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Inadequate sleep is a major cause of accidents by workers and poor performance by college students.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Driving while sleep deprived is comparable to driving under the influence of alcohol .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even one night of sleeplessness activates the immune system, as if you were ill .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h02","text":"Sleep and Energy Conservation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even if we agreed on what is the most important function of sleep for humans today, it might not be the function for which sleep originally evolved.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"All of those are valuable functions, but the original purpose of computers was to do mathematical calculations.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Similarly, sleep probably started with a simple function to which evolution added others later.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A likely hypothesis is that sleep’s original function, and still an important one, is to save energy .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep conserves energy during the times when activity would be ineffective and possibly dangerous.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When NASA built the Rover spacecraft to explore Mars, they included a mechanism to make it “sleep” at night to conserve the batteries.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, a mammal’s body temperature decreases by 1° or 2° C, enough to save a noticeable amount of energy.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Animals increase their sleep duration during food shortages, when energy conservation is especially important .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h03","text":"Analogous to Sleep: Hibernation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Hibernating animals decrease their body temperature, usually maintaining it just slightly above that of the environment, but always warm enough to prevent the blood from freezing.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heart rate and brain activity drop to almost nothing, neuron cell bodies shrink, and many synapses disappear, regenerating at the end of hibernation .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Here are a few curious facts about hibernation:","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h04","text":"Species Differences in Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If one of the main functions of sleep is to decrease activity at times of relative inefficiency, we might expect to find little or no sleep in species that are equally effective at all times of day.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast to the fish in normal waters, which average more than 13 hours of sleep per day, the populations in caves have only 2 to 4 hours of sleep per day without a circadian rhythm .","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many animals that live near the North or South Pole greatly decrease their sleep during summer, when the sun is constantly above the horizon.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Two elephant matriarchs, who take charge of protecting their troops, were observed to sleep two hours or less per night .","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To do so, they evolved the ability to sleep on one side of the brain at a time.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"These large birds never land on the water, because their feathers would become waterlogged and prevent them from taking flight again.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"EEG records indicate that they have periods of slow-wave sleep in one hemisphere at a time, and REM periods in both hemispheres.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Exactly how a mother dolphin, elephant matriarch, great frigate bird, or migratory bird decreases its sleep need is unknown, but the fact that it is possible fits with the idea that sleep is largely a way to conserve energy, and that the other functions of sleep can be performed briefly.","sourcePrintedPage":283,"sourcePdfPage":301,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Animals that need to be on the alert for predators get little sleep, whereas the predators themselves sleep easily.","sourcePrintedPage":283,"sourcePdfPage":301,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h05","text":"Sleep and Memory"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, if you learn something and then go to sleep, even a nap, your memory solidifies and may become better than it was before sleep .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another study found that a nap that included REM sleep enhanced performance on certain kinds of creative problem solving .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Both REM sleep and slow-wave sleep have been linked to strengthening of memories .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers recorded activity in the hippocampus during learning, and then recorded from the same locations during sleep, using microelectrodes within cells for laboratory animals and electrodes on the scalp for humans.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The results: Patterns that occurred during sleep resembled those that had occurred during learning, except that they were more rapid during sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As the brain replays its experiences during sleep it forms new dendritic branches that strengthen the memories .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Knowledge storage depends on highly synchronized sharp wave ripples that transfer information from the hippocampus","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An important way for sleep to strengthen memory is by weeding out the less successful connections.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research by Gina Poe and others has found that the brain conditions during sleep are ideal for pruning ineffective synapses and deleting unimportant memories .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h06","text":"Functions of REM Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"On average, people spend about a third of their life asleep and about a fifth of sleep in REM, totaling about 600 hours of REM per year.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One way to approach this question is to compare the people or animals with more REM to those with less.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"REM sleep is widespread in mammals and birds, indicating that it is part of our ancient evolutionary heritage.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As a rule, the species with the most total sleep hours also have the highest percentage of REM sleep .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cats spend up to 16 hours a day sleeping, much or most of it in REM sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, although memory consolidation does occur during REM, many people take antidepressant drugs that severely decrease REM sleep without causing memory problems .","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, because they are shielded from the air, they deteriorate slightly .","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"According to this view, REM is a way of arousing a sleeper just enough to shake the eyes back and forth, and the other manifestations of REM are just by-products.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This idea makes sense of the fact that REM occurs mostly toward the end of the night’s sleep, when the fluid behind the eyes would be the most stagnant.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h07","text":"Biological Perspectives on Dreaming"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dream research faces a special problem: All we know about dreams comes from people’s self-reports.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We forget most dreams, and even when we do remember them, the details fade quickly.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A common research procedure is to awaken people and ask for an immediate dream report.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h08","text":"The Activation-Synthesis Hypothesis"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"According to the activation-synthesis hypothesis , a dream represents the brain’s effort to make sense of sparse and distorted information.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dreams begin with periodic bursts of spontaneous activity in the pons—the PGO waves previously described—that activate parts of the cortex.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cortex combines this haphazard input with whatever other activity was already occurring and does its","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"best to synthesize a story that makes sense of the information .","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider how this theory handles a couple of common dreams.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Your brain in its partly aroused condition feels the vestibular sensation of your position and interprets it as flying or falling.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An interpretation based on the activation-synthesis theory is that during REM sleep (which accompanies most dreams), your motor cortex is inactive and your major postural muscles are virtually paralyzed.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The main objection is that most dreams have no apparent connection to any current stimuli .","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h09","text":"The Neurocognitive Model"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The neurocognitive model regards dreams as thinking that takes place under unusual conditions.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It emphasizes that dreams begin with spontaneous brain activity related to recent memories—just as most daytime thinking relates to recent memories .","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers used a PET scan to determine which brain areas increased or decreased their activity during REM, which is correlated with dreaming.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Further, a PET scan yields a clear image only if the head remains motionless during data collection.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They also inserted a cannula (plastic tube) into each person’s arm so that they could inject radioactive chemicals during the night.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the researchers foresaw the difficulty of sleeping under these conditions (!), they had their participants stay awake the entire previous night.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The upshot of all this is that the dreaming brain has little sensory input, leaving other brain areas free to generate images without constraints or interference.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the primary motor cortex is suppressed and the motor areas of the spinal cord are inhibited, arousal cannot lead to action.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Activity is suppressed in the prefrontal cortex, which is important for working memory and logical thinking.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Meanwhile, activity is relatively high in part of the parietal cortex important for visuospatial perception.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The idea behind the neurocognitive approach is that arousal of parts of the cerebral cortex develops into a hallucinatory perception, with no sensory input to override it.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A behavior can serve its function even when we do not fully understand that function.","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Nearly every species is more efficient at some times of day than at others.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299},{"type":"bullet","text":"The function of hibernation is simply to conserve energy while food is scarce.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299},{"type":"bullet","text":"Mexican cavefish have one population that lives in normal waters subject to alternations of day and night, and other populations that evolved to live in caves with no light and virtually constant temperature.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"While male sandpipers are competing for mates above the Arctic Circle, many of them are active up to 23 hours per day for nearly three weeks, with no apparent harm to their health or alertness.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"Seals also sleep in one hemisphere at a time when they are at sea, although they sleep in both hemispheres when they are on land.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"Moreover, their sleep episodes last an average of only 11 seconds, with a total of less than 45 minutes per night.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"Still, it gets little sleep, while remaining alert and performing normally on learning tasks.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":283,"sourcePdfPage":301},{"type":"bullet","text":"If the same bird is deprived of sleep during other seasons of the year, its performance suffers.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":283,"sourcePdfPage":301},{"type":"bullet","text":"If you do not get a good night’s sleep, your memory and cognition will suffer the next day.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"Sleep also helps people reanalyze their memories: In one study, people who had just practiced a complex task were more likely to perceive a hidden rule (an “aha” experience) after a period of sleep than after a similar period of wakefulness.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"If your brain strengthened synapses every time it learned something, without removing or weakening other synapses, the result might be runaway overactivity, or it might resemble the clutter in a room where you kept adding things without ever removing anything.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"Rabbits, guinea pigs, and sheep sleep less and spend little time in REM.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"Among young adults, those who sleep 9 or more hours per night have the highest percentage of REM sleep, and those who sleep 5 or fewer hours have the least percentage.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another hypothesis sounds odd because we tend to imagine a glamorous role for REM sleep: David Maurice (1998) proposed that REM just shakes the eyeballs back and forth enough to get sufficient oxygen to the corneas of the eyes.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303},{"type":"bullet","text":"It also fits with the fact that individuals who spend more hours asleep devote a greater percentage of sleep to REM.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303},{"type":"bullet","text":"While you are asleep, you lie flat, unlike your posture for the rest of the day.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h08","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"When you are dreaming, you really cannot move, you feel your lack of movement, and you dream of inability to move.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h08","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"To overcome these difficulties, researchers in two studies persuaded young people to sleep with their heads firmly attached to masks that did not permit any movement.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"You have a cannula in your arm and your head is locked into position.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"Consequently, you not only forget most dreams after you awaken, but you also lose track of what has been happening within a dream, and sudden scene changes are common.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"Remembering your dreams is not very useful (unless you plan to talk about them with your psychoanalyst), because you should not confuse dreams with reality.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"Without minimizing how much we do understand about sleep, it is noteworthy how many basic questions remain unanswered.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"Our lack of knowledge about activities that occupy so much of our time underscores a point about the biology of behavior: We evolved tendencies to behave in certain ways that lead to survival and reproduction.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"Without minimizing how much we do understand about sleep, it is noteworthy how many basic questions remain unanswered.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h10","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"Our lack of knowledge about activities that occupy so much of our time underscores a point about the biology of behavior: We evolved tendencies to behave in certain ways that lead to survival and reproduction.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h10","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"A behavior can serve its function even when we do not fully understand that function.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h10","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"Even if we agreed on what is the most important function of sleep for humans today, it might not be the function for which sleep originally evolved.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299},{"type":"bullet","text":"Hibernating animals decrease their body temperature, usually maintaining it just slightly above that of the environment, but always warm enough to prevent the blood from freezing.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299},{"type":"bullet","text":"If one of the main functions of sleep is to decrease activity at times of relative day.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"In contrast, if you learn something and then go to sleep, even a nap, your memory solidifies and may become better than it was before sleep .","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"According to the activation-synthesis hypothesis , a dream represents the brain’s effort to make sense of sparse and distorted information.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h07","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303},{"type":"bullet","text":"The perception.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":83},{"text":"The idea behind the neurocognitive approach is that arousal of parts of the cerebral cortex develops into a hallucinatory perception, with no sensory input to override .","printedPage":281,"pdfPage":299,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":21},{"text":"Sleep conserves energy during the times when activity would be .","printedPage":281,"pdfPage":299,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":25},{"text":"Nearly every species is more efficient at some times of day than at others.","printedPage":281,"pdfPage":299,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":86},{"text":"The function of hibernation is simply to conserve energy inefficiency, we might expect to find little or no sleep in species that are equally effective at all times of day.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":31},{"text":"In contrast to the fish in normal waters, which average more than 13 hours of sleep per day, the populations in caves have only 2 to 4 hours of sleep per day without a circadian rhythm .","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":32},{"text":"Many animals that live near the North or South Pole greatly decrease their sleep during summer, when the sun is constantly above the horizon.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":33},{"text":"Two elephant matriarchs, who take charge of protecting their troops, were observed to sleep two hours or less per night .","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":34},{"text":"To do so, they evolved the ability to sleep on one side of the brain at a time.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":35},{"text":"These large birds never land on the water, because their feathers would become waterlogged and prevent them from taking flight again.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":36},{"text":"EEG records indicate that they have periods of slow-wave sleep in one hemisphere at a time, and REM periods in both hemispheres.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":37},{"text":"Exactly how a mother dolphin, elephant matriarch, great frigate bird, or migratory bird decreases its sleep need is unknown, but the fact that it is possible fits with the idea that sleep is largely a way to conserve energy, and that the other functions of sleep can be performed briefly.","printedPage":283,"pdfPage":301,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":38},{"text":"Animals that need to be on the alert for predators get little sleep, whereas the predators themselves sleep easily.","printedPage":283,"pdfPage":301,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":39},{"text":"Mexican cavefish have one population that lives in normal waters subject to alternations of day and night, and other populations that evolved to live in caves with no light and virtually constant temperature.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":88},{"text":"While male sandpipers are competing for mates above the Arctic Circle, many of them are active up to 23 hours per day for nearly three weeks, with no apparent harm to their health or alertness.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":89},{"text":"Seals also sleep in one hemisphere at a time when they are at sea, although they sleep in both hemispheres when they are on land.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":90},{"text":"Moreover, their sleep episodes last an average of only 11 seconds, with a total of less than 45 minutes per night.","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":91},{"text":"Still, it gets little sleep, while remaining alert and performing normally on learning tasks.","printedPage":283,"pdfPage":301,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":92},{"text":"If the same bird is deprived of sleep during other seasons of the year, its performance suffers.","printedPage":283,"pdfPage":301,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":93}],"originalFacts":9,"additionalFacts":6,"glossary":[],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":933,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":394},{"id":"bp14-m8-3-h05","title":"Sleep .","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":42},{"text":"Both REM sleep and slow-wave sleep have been linked to strengthening of memories .","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":43},{"text":"Researchers recorded activity in the hippocampus during learning, and then recorded from the same locations during sleep, using microelectrodes within cells for laboratory animals and electrodes on the scalp for humans.","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":44},{"text":"The results: Patterns that occurred during sleep resembled those that had occurred during learning, except that they were more rapid during sleep.","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":45},{"text":"As the brain replays its experiences during sleep it forms new dendritic branches that strengthen the memories .","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":46},{"text":"Knowledge storage hippocampus","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":47},{"text":"An important way for sleep to strengthen memory is by weeding out the less successful connections.","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"Research by Gina Poe and others has found that the brain conditions during sleep are ideal for pruning ineffective synapses and deleting unimportant memories .","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":49},{"text":"If you do not get a good night’s sleep, your memory and cognition will suffer the next day.","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":94},{"text":"Sleep also helps people reanalyze their memories: In one study, people who had just practiced a complex task were more likely to perceive a hidden rule (an “aha” experience) after a period of sleep than after a similar period of wakefulness.","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":95},{"text":"If your brain strengthened synapses every time it learned something, without removing or weakening other synapses, the result might be runaway overactivity, or it might resemble the clutter in a room where you kept adding things without ever removing anything.","printedPage":284,"pdfPage":302,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":96}],"originalFacts":9,"additionalFacts":3,"glossary":[{"term":"Hippocampus","definition":"a .","printedPage":285,"pdfPage":303,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":56},{"text":"During sleep, because they are shielded from the air, they Driving while sleep deprived is comparable to driving under the influence of alcohol.","Even one night of sleeplessness activates the immune system, as if you were ill.","Even if we agreed on what is the most important function of sleep for humans today, it might not be the function for which sleep originally evolved.","All of those are valuable functions, but the original purpose of computers was to do mathematical calculations.","Similarly, sleep probably started with a simple function to which evolution added others later. A likely hypothesis is that sleep’s original function, and still an important one, is to save energy.","Sleep conserves energy during the times when activity would be ineffective and possibly dangerous.","When NASA built the Rover spacecraft to explore Mars, they included a mechanism to make it “sleep” at night to conserve the batteries.","During sleep, a mammal’s body temperature decreases by 1° or 2° C, enough to save a noticeable amount of energy. Animals increase their sleep duration during food shortages, when energy conservation is especially important.","Hibernation provides a useful comparison with sleep because both greatly reduce activity and conserve energy, but they are not the same state. In hibernation, body temperature can fall close to the surrounding temperature while remaining high enough to prevent freezing; heart rate and brain activity decline markedly.","Reducing activity and metabolism helps an animal survive periods when obtaining food would be difficult or inefficient. This is the main reason the textbook compares hibernation with sleep.","During hibernation, neuron cell bodies can shrink and many synapses disappear. These connections regenerate when hibernation ends, showing that the reduced state involves reversible neural changes.","If one of the main functions of sleep is to decrease activity at times of relative inefficiency, we might expect to find little or no sleep in species that are equally effective at all times of day.","In contrast to the fish in normal waters, which average more than 13 hours of sleep per day, the populations in caves have only 2 to 4 hours of sleep per day without a circadian rhythm.","Many animals that live near the North or South Pole greatly decrease their sleep during summer, when the sun is constantly above the horizon.","Two elephant matriarchs, who take charge of protecting their troops, were observed to sleep two hours or less per night. To do so, they evolved the ability to sleep on one side of the brain at a time.","These large birds never land on the water, because their feathers would become waterlogged and prevent them from taking flight again.","EEG records indicate that they have periods of slow-wave sleep in one hemisphere at a time, and REM periods in both hemispheres. Exactly how a mother dolphin, elephant matriarch, great frigate bird, or migratory bird decreases its sleep need is unknown, but the fact that it is possible fits with the idea that sleep is largely a way to conserve energy, and that the other functions of sleep can be performed briefly.","Animals that need to be on the alert for predators get little sleep, whereas the predators themselves sleep easily.","In contrast, if you learn something and then go to sleep, even a nap, your memory solidifies and may become better than it was before sleep.","Another study found that a nap that included REM sleep enhanced performance on certain kinds of creative problem solving.","Both REM sleep and slow-wave sleep have been linked to strengthening of memories.","Researchers recorded activity in the hippocampus during learning, and then recorded from the same locations during sleep, using microelectrodes within cells for laboratory animals and electrodes on the scalp for humans. The results: Patterns that occurred during sleep resembled those that had occurred during learning, except that they were more rapid during sleep.","As the brain replays its experiences during sleep it forms new dendritic branches that strengthen the memories.","Knowledge storage depends on highly synchronized sharp wave ripples that transfer information from the hippocampus An important way for sleep to strengthen memory is by weeding out the less successful connections.","Research by Gina Poe and others has found that the brain conditions during sleep are ideal for pruning ineffective synapses and deleting unimportant memories.","On average, people spend about a third of their life asleep and about a fifth of sleep in REM, totaling about 600 hours of REM per year.","One way to approach this question is to compare the people or animals with more REM to those with less.","REM sleep is widespread in mammals and birds, indicating that it is part of our ancient evolutionary heritage.","As a rule, the species with the most total sleep hours also have the highest percentage of REM sleep. Cats spend up to 16 hours a day sleeping, much or most of it in REM sleep.","However, although memory consolidation does occur during REM, many people take antidepressant drugs that severely decrease REM sleep without causing memory problems.","During sleep, because they are shielded from the air, they deteriorate slightly. According to this view, REM is a way of arousing a sleeper just enough to shake the eyes back and forth, and the other manifestations of REM are just by-products.","This idea makes sense of the fact that REM occurs mostly toward the end of the night’s sleep, when the fluid behind the eyes would be the most stagnant.","Dreaming is difficult to investigate because a dream is known mainly through the person’s report afterward. Memories of dreams fade quickly, and much of what was experienced may never be reported. This limits how directly researchers can connect brain activity during sleep with the content of dreams.","Researchers cannot observe a dream’s contents directly. They must infer those contents from what a person reports, sometimes after considerable forgetting.","A common approach is to wake a participant and ask what they were experiencing immediately before awakening. Shortening the delay may reduce some forgetting, but it does not make the report a direct recording of the dream.","According to the activation-synthesis hypothesis, a dream represents the brain’s effort to make sense of sparse and distorted information.","Dreams begin with periodic bursts of spontaneous activity in the pons—the PGO waves previously described—that activate parts of the cortex.","The cortex combines this haphazard input with whatever other activity was already occurring and does its best to synthesize a story that makes sense of the information.","Consider how this theory handles a couple of common dreams.","Your brain in its partly aroused condition feels the vestibular sensation of your position and interprets it as flying or falling.","An interpretation based on the activation-synthesis theory is that during REM sleep (which accompanies most dreams), your motor cortex is inactive and your major postural muscles are virtually paralyzed. The main objection is that most dreams have no apparent connection to any current stimuli.","The neurocognitive model regards dreams as thinking that takes place under unusual conditions.","It emphasizes that dreams begin with spontaneous brain activity related to recent memories—just as most daytime thinking relates to recent memories.","Researchers used a PET scan to determine which brain areas increased or decreased their activity during REM, which is correlated with dreaming. Further, a PET scan yields a clear image only if the head remains motionless during data collection.","They also inserted a cannula (plastic tube) into each person’s arm so that they could inject radioactive chemicals during the night.","Because the researchers foresaw the difficulty of sleeping under these conditions (!), they had their participants stay awake the entire previous night. The upshot of all this is that the dreaming brain has little sensory input, leaving other brain areas free to generate images without constraints or interference.","Because the primary motor cortex is suppressed and the motor areas of the spinal cord are inhibited, arousal cannot lead to action. Activity is suppressed in the prefrontal cortex, which is important for working memory and logical thinking.","Meanwhile, activity is relatively high in part of the parietal cortex important for visuospatial perception.","The idea behind the neurocognitive approach is that arousal of parts of the cerebral cortex develops into a hallucinatory perception, with no sensory input to override it. A behavior can serve its function even when we do not fully understand that function.","One important function of sleep is to conserve energy at times when the individual would be less efficient. Animal species vary in their sleep per day depending on their feeding habits and how much danger they face while asleep.","In addition to saving energy, sleep serves other functions, including enhancement of memory. REM sleep occupies the greatest percentage of sleep in the individuals and species that sleep the most total hours.","According to the activation-synthesis hypothesis, dreams are the brain’s attempts to make sense of the information reaching it, based mostly on haphazard input originating in the pons.","Normal sleep does not require the extreme reduction in body temperature and physiology seen in deep hibernation. The comparison is useful for thinking about energy conservation, not for treating both conditions as identical.","The text goes on to compare the activation-synthesis hypothesis and the neurocognitive model. These are proposed interpretations of dreaming and should be evaluated as explanations, not presented as established facts about every dream."],"classroomResearch":{"title":"Evidence in context: Sleep Self-Understanding","printedPage":287,"additionalStudyPoints":[],"sourceBodyWords":0,"addedWords":0,"sourceParagraphs":0}],"masterclassCount":2},{"id":"bp14-m9-1","chapterId":"bp14-ch09","moduleId":"bp14-m9-1","moduleNumber":"9.1","title":"Temperature Regulation","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":292,"printedEnd":299,"pdfStart":310,"pdfEnd":317,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Body temperature is regulated by physiological mechanisms and behavior. Homeostasis and allostasis frame how the body maintains useful conditions while preparing for changing demands."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The discussion includes endothermy, survival in cold environments, brain mechanisms, and fever. Compare immediate temperature responses with the longer-term regulatory systems that coordinate them."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-1-study-1","text":"Homeostasis versus allostasis"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The body regulates variables such as temperature through feedback mechanisms. Homeostasis describes processes that keep internal conditions within useful ranges, often by correcting deviations. Allostasis emphasizes adjustments that anticipate or respond to changing demands rather than holding every value fixed at one number. Regulation involves both physiological reactions and behavior. Seeking shelter or changing clothes can be as important as shifting blood flow or producing heat."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-1-study-2","text":"Endothermy has a cost and a benefit"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Maintaining a relatively high body temperature requires substantial energy, but it allows enzymes, muscles, and neural processes to operate reliably across changing external temperatures. Different species balance energy expenditure and environmental dependence in different ways. Humans combine physiological temperature regulation with purposeful actions, so understanding thermoregulation demands more than memorizing the body's average temperature."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-1-study-3","text":"Brain and body mechanisms"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Temperature-sensitive signals influence hypothalamic and other central systems that alter sweating, shivering, peripheral blood flow, and motivated behavior. In cold conditions, the body may conserve heat and generate more; in heat, it may promote heat loss. These responses interact and can be overridden or constrained by environmental conditions. Extremely cold situations challenge regulatory capacity and may require behavioral strategies for survival."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-1-study-4","text":"Fever is regulated, not random heat"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Fever can involve a change in the level at which the body defends temperature during an immune response. This is different from simply overheating because heat cannot be removed. A moderate fever may support aspects of defense against infection, while excessive temperature is harmful. The broader lesson is that bodily regulation reflects trade-offs: a response that provides some advantage also has physiological costs."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-1-h01","text":"Homeostasis and Allostasis"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cannon introduced the term homeostasis (HO-mee-oh-STAY-sis) to refer to biological processes that keep body variables within a fixed range.","sourcePrintedPage":293,"sourcePdfPage":311,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When the temperature drops below the minimum, the thermostat triggers the furnace to provide heat.","sourcePrintedPage":293,"sourcePdfPage":311,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When the temperature rises above the maximum, the thermostat turns on the air conditioner.","sourcePrintedPage":293,"sourcePdfPage":311,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Homeostatic processes in animals trigger physiological and behavioral activities that keep variables within a set range.","sourcePrintedPage":293,"sourcePdfPage":311,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sometimes the range is so narrow that we call it a set point , a single value that the body works to maintain.","sourcePrintedPage":293,"sourcePdfPage":311,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Similar mechanisms maintain constant blood levels of water, oxygen, glucose, sodium chloride, protein, fat, and acidity .","sourcePrintedPage":293,"sourcePdfPage":311,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Much of motivated behavior can be described as negative feedback: Something causes a disturbance, and behavior proceeds until it relieves the disturbance.","sourcePrintedPage":293,"sourcePdfPage":311,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When the air starts to warm up, a hiker increases thirst and decreases urine production by the kidneys, anticipating probable sweating and dehydration.","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To describe these dynamic changes, researchers use the term allostasis (from the Greek roots meaning “variable” and “standing”), which means the way in which the body anticipates needs, avoiding errors rather than correcting them .","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-1-h02","text":"Controlling Body Temperature"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most of it goes to basal metabolism , the energy used to maintain a constant body temperature while at rest.","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For most people, maintaining body temperature uses about twice as much energy as all the muscle activity, brain activity, and everything else combined .","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A synonym is poikilothermic, from Greek roots meaning “varied heat.” An ectothermic animal’s body temperature is nearly the same as the temperature of its environment.","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A desert lizard moves between sunny areas, shady areas, and burrows to keep body temperature almost constant.","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, behavioral methods do not achieve the same degree of constancy that mammals and birds have.","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A few large fish, including sharks and tuna, maintain their core body temperature well above that of the surrounding water most of the time .","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The tegu lizards of South America, about the size of a large rabbit, increase their metabolism during the mating season, raising their body temperature to sometimes 10°C above that of the environment .","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, if the air is humid as well as hot, the moisture does not evaporate.","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They risk dehydration, a dangerously high body temperature, heat exhaustion, and organ damage .","sourcePrintedPage":294,"sourcePdfPage":312,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-1-h03","text":"Surviving in Extreme Cold"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If its body temperature drops below the freezing point of water, ice crystals form.","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because water expands when it freezes, ice crystals would tear apart blood vessels and cell membranes, killing the animal.","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many amphibians and reptiles avoid that risk by burrowing or finding other sheltered locations.","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, some frogs, fish, and insects survive through winters in northern Canada where even the underground temperature approaches –40°C (which is also –40°F).","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some insects and fish stock their blood with glycerol and other antifreeze chemicals at the start of the winter .","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Wood frogs in Canada and Alaska actually do freeze, but they have mechanisms to reduce the damage.","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They start by withdrawing most fluid from their organs and blood vessels and storing it in extracellular spaces.","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Therefore, ice crystals have room to expand when they form, without tearing blood vessels or cells.","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Also, the frogs have chemicals that cause ice crystals to form gradually, not in chunks.","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-1-h04","text":"The Advantages of Endothermy"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As mentioned, we spend about two-thirds of our total energy maintaining body temperature (basal metabolism).","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Maintaining body temperature must provide an important advantage, or we would not have evolved these energy-expensive mechanisms.","sourcePrintedPage":295,"sourcePdfPage":313,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Birds and mammals keep warm at all times and therefore stay constantly ready for vigorous activity, regardless of the air temperature.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Second, and more importantly, beyond about 41°C (105°F), most proteins begin to break their bonds and lose their useful properties.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, to do so, they need many extra chemical bonds to stabilize their proteins.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In short, our body temperature of 37°C is a trade-off between the advantages of high temperature for rapid movement and the disadvantages of high temperature for protein stability.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Birds lay eggs and sit on them, instead of developing them internally, because the birds’ internal temperature is too hot for an embryo.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Similarly, in most male mammals, the scrotum hangs outside the body, because sperm production requires a cooler temperature than the rest of the body. (It’s not just for decoration.) A man who wears his undershorts too tight keeps his testes too close to the body, overheats them, and produces fewer healthy sperm cells.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-1-h05","text":"Brain Mechanisms"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Behavioral methods of temperature regulation, such as finding a cooler or warmer place, also depend on the hypothalamus .","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Physiological regulation depends mainly on the anterior hypothalamus and the preoptic area, located just anterior to the anterior hypothalamus.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It is called preoptic because it is near the optic chiasm, where the optic nerves cross.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of the close relationship between the preoptic area and the anterior hypothalamus, researchers often treat them as a single area, the preoptic area/anterior hypothalamus , or POA/AH .","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The POA/AH receives input from temperature receptors in the skin and organs, and about 30 percent of the neurons in the POA/AH sense changes in their own temperature .","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If either the skin or the hypothalamus is hot, an animal sweats or pants vigorously and seeks a cooler location.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After damage to the POA/AH, mammals regulate body temperature mainly by the behavioral mechanisms that a lizard might use, such as seeking a warmer or colder location .","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-1-h06","text":"Fever"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The body reacts by shivering and other processes that produce a fever. .","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In other words, fever is something the hypothalamus directs the body to produce.","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People lacking the receptors for prostaglandins and histamines fail to develop a fever, even if they have pneumonia","sourcePrintedPage":296,"sourcePdfPage":314,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because newborn rabbits have an immature hypothalamus, they do not shiver in response to infections.","sourcePrintedPage":297,"sourcePdfPage":315,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If they are given a choice of environments, however, they select a spot warm enough to raise their body temperature","sourcePrintedPage":297,"sourcePdfPage":315,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Fish and reptiles with an infection also choose a warm enough environment, if they can find one, to produce a feverish body temperature .","sourcePrintedPage":297,"sourcePdfPage":315,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Again, the point is that fever is something the animal does to fight an infection.","sourcePrintedPage":297,"sourcePdfPage":315,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Other things being equal, developing a moderate fever increases an individual’s chance of surviving a bacterial infection .","sourcePrintedPage":298,"sourcePdfPage":316,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, a fever above .","printedPage":294,"pdfPage":312,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":22},{"text":"A synonym is poikilothermic, from Greek roots meaning “varied heat.” body temperature well above that of the surrounding water most of the time .","printedPage":294,"pdfPage":312,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":26},{"text":"The tegu lizards of South America, about the size of a large rabbit, .","printedPage":294,"pdfPage":312,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":27},{"text":"However, if the air is humid as well as hot, the moisture does not constant.","printedPage":294,"pdfPage":312,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"They need much fuel each day to maintain their body smarter than form.","printedPage":295,"pdfPage":313,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":31},{"text":"Because water expands when it freezes, ice crystals would tear amphibians and reptiles avoid that risk by burrowing or finding other sheltered locations.","printedPage":295,"pdfPage":313,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":33},{"text":"However, some frogs, fish, and insects survive through winters in northern Canada where even the underground temperature approaches –40°C (which is also –40°F).","printedPage":295,"pdfPage":313,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":34},{"text":"Some insects and fish stock their blood with glycerol and other antifreeze chemicals at the start of the winter .","printedPage":295,"pdfPage":313,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":35},{"text":"Wood frogs in Canada and Alaska actually do freeze, but they have mechanisms to reduce the cells.","printedPage":295,"pdfPage":313,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":38},{"text":"Also, the frogs have chemicals that cause ice crystals to form forth.","printedPage":295,"pdfPage":313,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":83},{"text":"An ectothermic animal, which necessarily takes the trade-off between the advantages of high temperature for rapid movement and the disadvantages of high temperature for protein stability.","printedPage":296,"pdfPage":314,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":46},{"text":"Birds lay eggs and sit on them, instead of developing them internally, because the birds’ internal temperature is too hot for an (It’s not just for decoration.) A man who wears his undershorts too tight keeps his testes too close to the body, overheats them, and produces fewer healthy sperm cells.","printedPage":296,"pdfPage":314,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"If we didn’t maintain a constant, high body temperature, we the chapter on movement: As the water gets colder, a fish recruits more and more fast-twitch muscle fibers to remain active, running the risk of rapid fatigue.","printedPage":295,"pdfPage":313,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":86},{"text":"Let’s qualify this point just a bit: On a cold day, you air.","printedPage":296,"pdfPage":314,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":87},{"text":"Indeed, odd microscopic animals called thermophiles survive .","printedPage":296,"pdfPage":314,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":56},{"text":"The physiological changes that regulate body temperature— such as Sometimes the range is so narrow that we call it a set point, a single value that the body works to maintain.","Similar mechanisms maintain constant blood levels of water, oxygen, glucose, sodium chloride, protein, fat, and acidity.","Much of motivated behavior can be described as negative feedback: Something causes a disturbance, and behavior proceeds until it relieves the disturbance. When the air starts to warm up, a hiker increases thirst and decreases urine production by the kidneys, anticipating probable sweating and dehydration.","To describe these dynamic changes, researchers use the term allostasis (from the Greek roots meaning “variable” and “standing”), which means the way in which the body anticipates needs, avoiding errors rather than correcting them.","Most of it goes to basal metabolism, the energy used to maintain a constant body temperature while at rest.","For most people, maintaining body temperature uses about twice as much energy as all the muscle activity, brain activity, and everything else combined.","A synonym is poikilothermic, from Greek roots meaning “varied heat.” An ectothermic animal’s body temperature is nearly the same as the temperature of its environment.","A desert lizard moves between sunny areas, shady areas, and burrows to keep body temperature almost constant. However, if the air is humid as well as hot, the moisture does not evaporate.","They risk dehydration, a dangerously high body temperature, heat exhaustion, and organ damage.","If its body temperature drops below the freezing point of water, ice crystals form.","Because water expands when it freezes, ice crystals would tear apart blood vessels and cell membranes, killing the animal.","Many amphibians and reptiles avoid that risk by burrowing or finding other sheltered locations.","However, some frogs, fish, and insects survive through winters in northern Canada where even the underground temperature approaches –40°C (which is also –40°F). Some insects and fish stock their blood with glycerol and other antifreeze chemicals at the start of the winter.","Wood frogs in Canada and Alaska actually do freeze, but they have mechanisms to reduce the damage.","They start by withdrawing most fluid from their organs and blood vessels and storing it in extracellular spaces. Therefore, ice crystals have room to expand when they form, without tearing blood vessels or cells.","Also, the frogs have chemicals that cause ice crystals to form gradually, not in chunks.","As mentioned, we spend about two-thirds of our total energy maintaining body temperature (basal metabolism).","Maintaining body temperature must provide an important advantage, or we would not have evolved these energy-expensive mechanisms.","Birds and mammals keep warm at all times and therefore stay constantly ready for vigorous activity, regardless of the air temperature. Second, and more importantly, beyond about 41°C (105°F), most proteins begin to break their bonds and lose their useful properties.","However, to do so, they need many extra chemical bonds to stabilize their proteins.","In short, our body temperature of 37°C is a trade-off between the advantages of high temperature for rapid movement and the disadvantages of high temperature for protein stability.","Birds lay eggs and sit on them, instead of developing them internally, because the birds’ internal temperature is too hot for an embryo. Similarly, in most male mammals, the scrotum hangs outside the body, because sperm production requires a cooler temperature than the rest of the body. (It’s not just for decoration.) A man who wears his undershorts too tight keeps his testes too close to the body, overheats them, and produces fewer healthy sperm cells.","Behavioral methods of temperature regulation, such as finding a cooler or warmer place, also depend on the hypothalamus.","Physiological regulation depends mainly on the anterior hypothalamus and the preoptic area, located just anterior to the anterior hypothalamus.","It is called preoptic because it is near the optic chiasm, where the optic nerves cross. Because of the close relationship between the preoptic area and the anterior hypothalamus, researchers often treat them as a single area, the preoptic area/anterior hypothalamus, or POA/AH.","The POA/AH receives input from temperature receptors in the skin and organs, and about 30 percent of the neurons in the POA/AH sense changes in their own temperature.","If either the skin or the hypothalamus is hot, an animal sweats or pants vigorously and seeks a cooler location. After damage to the POA/AH, mammals regulate body temperature mainly by the behavioral mechanisms that a lizard might use, such as seeking a warmer or colder location.","The body reacts by shivering and other processes that produce a fever..","In other words, fever is something the hypothalamus directs the body to produce.","People lacking the receptors for prostaglandins and histamines fail to develop a fever, even if they have pneumonia","Because newborn rabbits have an immature hypothalamus, they do not shiver in response to infections. If they are given a choice of environments, however, they select a spot warm enough to raise their body temperature","Fish and reptiles with an infection also choose a warm enough environment, if they can find one, to produce a feverish body temperature.","Again, the point is that fever is something the animal does to fight an infection. Other things being equal, developing a moderate fever increases an individual’s chance of surviving a bacterial infection.","However, a fever above about 39°C (103°F) in humans does more harm than good,","Your body has physiological mechanisms to maintain constant body temperature, including shivering, sweating, and changes in blood flow, but you also rely on behavioral mechanisms, such as finding a cooler or warmer place, changing clothing, and so forth.","Redundancy reduces your risk: If one mechanism fails, another mechanism comes to your rescue.","We shall see this theme again in the discussions of thirst and hunger.","and a fever above 41°C (106°F) is life-threatening.
