reflects more than the sensation of a dry mouth. Osmotic thirst responds to changes in fluid concentration, while hypovolemic thirst follows losses of fluid volume; sodium-specific hunger is related but distinct."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The brain and hormones coordinate water balance with drinking behavior. Pay attention to how the book differentiates water replacement from replacing both water and salts."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-2-study-1","text":"Thirst is not one single signal"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Fluid regulation protects blood volume and the concentration of dissolved substances. Osmotic thirst arises when body fluids become too concentrated, creating a need for water relative to solutes. Hypovolemic thirst arises when fluid volume is reduced, as can happen after losing blood or substantial fluid. The two conditions can overlap but rely on partly distinct detection and hormonal pathways. This distinction explains why thirst cannot be interpreted solely as a dry mouth."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-2-study-2","text":"Hormones and the kidneys"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Antidiuretic hormone (ADH, also called vasopressin) helps the kidneys conserve water by allowing more water to be reabsorbed. Other hormonal and neural mechanisms respond to changes in blood volume and pressure. The brain combines these signals with information about the mouth, stomach, and availability of water to organize drinking behavior. Physiological regulation and the decision to drink are connected but are not identical processes."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-2-study-3","text":"Why salt matters"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Losing extracellular fluid can also produce sodium-specific hunger, a motivation to obtain salt as well as water. Drinking plain water alone is not always the complete solution to restoring fluid balance. The precise motivational response depends on what kind of deficit the body detects. Compare a person who has consumed very salty food with a person who has lost both water and sodium: their physiological needs differ even if both report thirst."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m9-2-study-4","text":"A compact way to revise"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For each form of thirst, answer four questions: What changed in body fluids? Which receptors or systems detect the change? Which hormonal or neural responses follow? What behavior restores balance? The key contrast is concentration versus volume, while acknowledging that natural situations may engage both mechanisms."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-2-h01","text":"Strategies of Water Regulation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Species differ in their strategies for maintaining water.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Beavers and other animals that live in rivers or lakes drink plenty of water, eat moist foods, and excrete dilute urine.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Gerbils and other desert animals can go through life without drinking at all.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They gain water from their food, and they retain water by excreting dry feces and concentrated urine.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Unable to sweat, they avoid the heat of the day by burrowing under the ground.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Yellowbellied sea snakes of the Indian and Pacific oceans require fresh water to survive.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They get it by drinking rainwater that falls at the top of the ocean during the rainy season, and then they conserve that water during the dry season that can last more than half a year .","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"blood vessels. (The term vasopressin comes from vas cular press ure.) The increased pressure helps compensate for the decreased blood volume.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-2-h02","text":"Osmotic Thirst"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The membrane surrounding a cell is almost a semipermeable membrane, because water flows across it freely and various solutes flow either slowly or not at all.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The result is a higher concentration of solutes outside the cells than inside, and the resulting osmotic pressure draws water from the cells into the extracellular fluid.","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When these neurons detect increased osmotic pressure by noting their own loss of water, they trigger osmotic thirst , a drive for water that helps restore the normal state (Figure 9.9).","sourcePrintedPage":301,"sourcePdfPage":319,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In reaction to osmotic thirst, the lateral preoptic area and surrounding parts of the hypothalamus increase drinking , while the supraoptic nucleus and paraventricular nucleus (PVN) stimulate the posterior pituitary to release vasopressin.","sourcePrintedPage":301,"sourcePdfPage":319,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The vasopressin also inhibits your need to urinate and therefore enables you to get through the night without becoming dehydrated.","sourcePrintedPage":301,"sourcePdfPage":319,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The OVLT also receives input from the tongue, and each lick of water decreases thirst by a tiny amount, long before the blood could distribute the water to reduce osmotic pressure .","sourcePrintedPage":301,"sourcePdfPage":319,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Receptors in the circulation to the liver detect the osmotic concentration of the fluid, and if it is low, they signal the brain to decrease thirst .","sourcePrintedPage":301,"sourcePdfPage":319,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m9-2-h03","text":"Hypovolemic Thirst and Sodium-Specific Hunger"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Those areas have some cells that detect osmotic pressure, some that respond to blood volume, and a few that are sensitive to both .","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Angiotensin II also triggers thirst, in conjunction with receptors that detect blood pressure in the large veins.","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, thirst caused by low blood volume, known as hypovolemic (HI-po-vo-LEE-mik) thirst , differs from osmotic thirst, because you need to restore lost salts and not just water.","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When angiotensin II reaches the brain, it stimulates neurons that release angiotensin II as a neuromodulator .","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That is, neurons regulating hypovolemic thirst both respond to angiotensin II and release it.","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Whereas an animal with osmotic thirst needs water, one with hypovolemic thirst cannot drink much pure water.","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The animal therefore increases its preference for salty water .","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Deficiency in sodium provokes sodium-specific hunger , a drive to consume salty tastes .","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When the body’s sodium reserves are low, the adrenal glands release the hormone aldosterone (al-DOSSter-one) that causes the kidneys, salivary glands, and sweat glands to retain salt .","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Therefore, he was constantly excreting sodium and he needed to ingest it constantly to replenish his supplies .","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Either one by itself produces only a small increase in sodium intake, but their combined effect is substantial, .","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Their convoluted nasal passages minimize water loss when they exhale.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318},{"type":"bullet","text":"If you cannot find enough to drink or if the water tastes bad, you conserve water by excreting more concentrated urine and decreasing your sweat, somewhat like a gerbil, although not to the same extreme.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318},{"type":"bullet","text":"Vasopressin is also known as antidiuretic hormone (ADH) because it enables the kidneys to reabsorb water from urine and make the urine more concentrated.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318},{"type":"bullet","text":"( Diuresis means “urination.”) When water is available, our strategy is closer to that of beavers: We drink more than we need and excrete the excess.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318},{"type":"bullet","text":"The combined concentration of all solutes in mammalian body fluids remains at a nearly constant level of 0.15 M (molar).","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318},{"type":"bullet","text":"(A 1.0 M solution of sugar and a 1.0 M solution of sodium chloride have the same number of molecules per liter.) This fixed concentration of solutes is a set point, like the set point for temperature.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318},{"type":"bullet","text":"Osmotic pressure is the tendency of water to flow across a semipermeable membrane from an area of low solute concentration to an area of higher concentration.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":300,"sourcePdfPage":318},{"type":"bullet","text":"Receptors in areas around the third ventricle, including the OVLT (organum vasculosum laminae terminalis) and the subfornical organ (SFO) detect osmotic pressure and the sodium content of the blood.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":301,"sourcePdfPage":319},{"type":"bullet","text":"As a result, you feel an urge to drink something, even if your cells’ osmotic pressure is normal at the time.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":301,"sourcePdfPage":319},{"type":"bullet","text":"After you eat or drink, changes in blood osmotic pressure take time, but you adjust your thirst long before that takes place.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":301,"sourcePdfPage":319},{"type":"bullet","text":"If you lose a significant amount of body fluid by bleeding, diarrhea, or sweating, your body’s osmotic pressure stays the same, but you need fluid.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320},{"type":"bullet","text":"Receptors in your kidneys and on your blood vessels react to the decreased blood pressure by sending messages to the OVLT and the SFO— the same areas that respond to osmotic thirst.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320},{"type":"bullet","text":"He demanded a layer of salt on everything he ate, and he ate salt directly from the shaker.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":302,"sourcePdfPage":320},{"type":"bullet","text":"You control your body temperature partly by automatic means, such as sweating or shivering, but also partly by behavioral means, such as choosing a warm or a cool place.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":303,"sourcePdfPage":321},{"type":"bullet","text":"If your kidneys cannot regulate your water and sodium adequately, your brain gets signals to change your drinking or sodium intake.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":303,"sourcePdfPage":321},{"type":"bullet","text":"An injection of concentrated sodium chloride triggers osmotic thirst, but equally concentrated glucose does not.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":303,"sourcePdfPage":321},{"type":"bullet","text":"You may have thought that temperature regulation happens automatically, and that water regulation depends on your behavior.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":303,"sourcePdfPage":321},{"type":"bullet","text":"You can see now that the distinction is not entirely correct.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":303,"sourcePdfPage":321},{"type":"bullet","text":"You control your body temperature partly by automatic means, such as sweating or shivering, but also partly by behavioral means, such as choosing a warm or a cool place.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":303,"sourcePdfPage":321},{"type":"bullet","text":"You control your body water partly by the behavior of drinking but also by hormones that alter kidney activity.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":303,"sourcePdfPage":321},{"type":"bullet","text":"If your kidneys cannot regulate your water and sodium adequately, your brain gets signals to change your drinking or sodium intake.","headingId":"bp14-m9-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":303,"sourcePdfPage":321},{"type":"bullet","text":"Keeping your body’s chemical reactions going depends on both skeletal and autonomic
